description: Screen Wake Lock outcomes (B10, WebCore #118). Chromium values come from tests/abi/wake_lock_browser.mjs; native values from tests/abi/wake_locks.py. A qualified case records where the engines differ and why.

ungranted-request.note: Chromium without the screen-wake-lock permission; native with a host policy that denies

detached-request.qualification: A native host has one document and no frames, so no detached document can request; a destroyed host is not a valid argument.

document-teardown.qualification: WebKit releases every lock when the document stops (Document::stopActiveDOMObjects) and fires no release event in a stopped context; Chromium leaves released false on the detached sentinel. Neither engine fires an event.

permissions-policy-none.qualification: A native host document has no response headers or iframes; rv_wake_lock_request still evaluates the screen-wake-lock policy feature, which a top-level native document allows.

hidden-release.qualification: Automated Chromium keeps every page visible (headless and headed, minimized or behind another tab), so the hidden-document release is native-only evidence.
